newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on large exports, fund buying.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on large exports, fund buying.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on European exporter buying, fund buying and commission stop loss buying, traders said.

"There was 20 to 40,000 tonnes of business done to Europe, there was heavy stop loss buying and funds bought 250 to 300 November late in the day," a trader said. Japan bought 5,000 tonnes overnight. Sep-Nov spread at $6.90, Jan-Mar $3.50, Nov-Jan $5. Volume was heavy at 6,925 lots, or 138,500 tonnes.
September canola climbed $3.50 to end at $423.80, November was up $3.50 to $430.30 and January was up $4 to $435.70.
October flax up $1.50 to $382.50 on commercials, November up $0.50 to $358. Volume 585.

"There was good commercial and commission buying of feed grains, short covering into the close. It doesn't make sense on a harvest weekend but we've been down all week so there's been cash trade," a trader said.

November western barley rose $1.10 to $149.30, February was up $1.40 to $154.50. Volume was 750. October wheat up $1.10 to $201.50, December up $0.80 to $187.50. Oct-Dec spread $14.50. Volume was 400. Oats did not trade.
October feed peas rose US$3.80 to US$209.80. Dec up US$2.50 to US$210 on a strong cash market. Volume was 215.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
